description:
causal::Cause (Initial/Content/Readiness/Uncaused) and scheduler::WorkStartReason (Ignition/ChangedRevisionWake/ActivationFrontier/BlockedWaiterExpansion/Unclassified) are the same question -- why did this run -- answered twice, in two vocabularies, by two components at two times, one decided and one inferred.

The tell: Uncaused and Unclassified are both the no-sanctioned-reason bucket, and both are asserted zero by separate mechanisms -- unsanctioned_work_starts() == 0 and 'zero uncaused evaluations' on the target fixtures. One invariant, two proofs, two models kept in agreement by hand.

## Readiness is NOT a second axis -- resolved

An earlier draft of this ticket worried that Readiness (settledness flipped, no revision moved) might not map onto a single WorkStartReason and could be a genuine second axis. Investigation settles it: it is not.

FactUse is Current(F) | Settled(F), and a wake's cause IS a FactUse, already serialized as "use":"current" / "use":"settled". So content-vs-readiness is a property of the emitted cause, not something needing separate modelling:
  Current-use wake  -> Content
  Settled-use wake  -> Readiness

causal.rs already believes this. woken_by_settled cross-checks every derived Readiness against an actual Settled-use wake in the window, and readiness_without_settled_wake.is_empty() is asserted in public_trace_test (twice) and tests/fz2_cli.rs. Non-vacuous: readiness_caused: 6 is pinned in a fixture, guarded by an explicit executable_fact_readiness > 0 assertion.

So the classification axis is (WorkStartReason, FactUse discriminant), both already on the wake. Delete Cause; the report reads them.

Do not force data into WorkStartReason: it is Copy and used as a tally map key.

Reconcile the two zero-assertions into one.
title: Fold Cause into one vocabulary for why work ran
